title: Libyan army says 2 officers were killed in Ukraine's attack on Russian warship
summary: Two Libyan naval officers died from wounds sustained in Ukraine's recent drone attack on a Russian warship docked at a port in eastern Libya, military authorities there said, vowing unspecified…

blocks.text: World

Two Libyan naval officers died from wounds sustained in Ukraine's recent drone attack on a Russian warship docked at a port in eastern Libya, military authorities there said, vowing unspecified retaliation against Kyiv for the deaths.
Vows to retaliate 'at the appropriate time and place'
Ukraine’s attack on Russian ship off Libya showcases drone, intelligence capabilities

The two men were pronounced dead Tuesday evening after being wounded when a sea drone struck the corvette Merkury at the Benghazi Naval Base, where it was refuelling and resupplying, the Libyan National Army (LNA) said in a statement.
The LNA's general command vowed to retaliate "at the appropriate time and place, and by the appropriate means."

Commanded by Gen. Khalifa Hifter, the LNA is the most powerful group in Libya, a country fractured by years of civil war and chaos. Hifter is backed by Moscow, and the LNA controls eastern and southern parts of the country. A rival and more broadly recognized government based in Tripoli controls the west — from where the drone attack reportedly was launched.
Meanwhile, Russia continued attacking Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter, while Kyiv reported further strikes on Russian oil refineries.
An overnight Russian attack on the Kyiv region killed one person, Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Wednesday.
Russia launched 112 drones, more than half of them jet-powered, with strikes hitting 18 locations, Ukraine's air force said. Authorities reported power outages in five regions.
Rescuers and a resident remove debris from an apartment building damaged by a Russian military strike in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, on Wednesday. (Reuters)
Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces intercepted 305 Ukrainian drones over several regions overnight.
Ukraine's Security Service said it struck two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region, setting both ablaze. Russian officials did not confirm the strikes.
The two refineries have a combined processing capacity of about 117 million barrels a year, the service said.

A screen recording shows the moment of the attack on the Russian cargo ship MV Angara, off the coast of Benghazi, Libya, on Sunday, in this screengrab taken from a video. (Libyan National Army/Reuters)

Ukrainian forces are operating in western Libya under a covert deal endorsed by the West, using the North African country's territory to strike a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in March, according to Libyan officials who spoke at the time.

Ukrainian officials offered no immediate response Wednesday, though they insisted the previous day that Kyiv's forces hadn't targeted Libyans in the operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres from the war's front line.

As well, Ukraine Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said that both Russian naval vessels and cargo ships transporting military equipment were valid targets and claimed that Ukraine's right to self-defence was enshrined in Article 51 of the United Nations Charter.
At least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded in the attack, according to a Libyan official.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said that no country leaves "any attempt on the life of its military unpunished." He declined to comment on Russian personnel reportedly wounded in the attack.

The attack brought the Russia-Ukraine war to a new battleground. The Libyan deaths stoked tensions over Kyiv's daring attack and added a new dimension to fears that Europe's biggest conflict since the Second World War is spreading farther beyond Ukraine.
The Tripoli-based government has cultivated ties with Ukraine and its Western allies, partly to support its efforts to stay in power.
Since Russia invaded its neighbour nearly five years ago, political, diplomatic and economic fallout from the war has been felt far beyond Ukraine's borders, now including North Africa.

blocks.text: The war has prompted European countries to spend billions on improving its defences, especially as questions have arisen about the U.S. government's commitment to Ukraine.

Western officials have accused Russia of staging dozens of cyberattacks and other acts of sabotage across Europe, striking cargo vessels in the Black Sea off the coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria, and deliberately violating European airspace.
Russia and Ukraine have traded increasingly damaging long-range attacks, even as they engage in U.S.-mediated talks that so far have done nothing to stop the fighting.

An initial investigation found that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched against the Merkury from a base operated by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to two officials, who were briefed on the investigation.
At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed in Sunday's attack, while two struck the corvette, which is designed to patrol coastal waters and escort other vessels, local officials said.
The officials, who are affiliated with the LNA, spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters.
With files from CBC News and Reuters
